{"version": 1, "content": "

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the list in the note above.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Qwen Image 2.1) - The image model itself, 7B, from Alibaba's Qwen team.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL 8B) - Reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE - Turns pictures into the model's own format and back. It works with four channels, red, green, blue and transparency, which is how this model can hand back a transparent picture.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma - Adds the Consistency LoRA, right after the model loader. It keeps the edit on your picture's own frame, so nothing moves or stretches. It has no trigger word and runs at strength 1. Switch its row off to see what plain Qwen does.

 The numbers you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you have to touch.

  • 1. Load Image - The picture you are editing. The result keeps its shape.
  • 2. Output Size - How many pixels the result has. Pick a line from the list: 1024 is about 1 megapixel and fast, 2048 is Qwen's native 2K and much slower. Your picture keeps its shape either way.
  • 3. Add a prompt - What to change. The LoRA helps most when the whole picture changes, like a painting style, because that is where plain Qwen moves things around.
  • 4. Seed Random/Fixed? - Fixed repeats the same result, Random rolls a new one each Run.

 The speed nodes

Teal, above the graph.

  • Qwen Image 2.1 Cache - Where the model keeps what it has already worked out about your picture and the prompt, so it does not redo that on every step. Leave it on auto / default. The note on the right says when to change it.
  • Model Attention Backend - Set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the model's attention maths. It changes the speed, not the picture. On a graphics card that cannot use it, ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself.

 The helpers

Purple. They run by themselves.

  • Scale Image to Total Pixels - Works out the exact size the model uses at the Output Size you picked: that many pixels, in steps of 32, in your picture's shape. Only that size is used.
  • Get Image Size - Reads that size as a width and a height for Resize Crop Pixaroma under it.
  • Resize Crop Pixaroma - Scales your picture to that size and crops the few pixels that do not fit, so the model edits a picture exactly the size of the result. Nothing is stretched, and the result lines up with your picture in the Compare.

 The render

Green. These run by themselves.

  • Text Encode Qwen Image 2.1 - Reads your prompt and your picture. Its resolution is set to 0, which takes it as it comes, already sized by the helpers. It also makes the blank canvas for the result at that size, which is why there is no separate latent node. Its negative prompt box does nothing at CFG 1, the setting this model is made for, so leave it empty.
  • KSampler - The render: 25 steps, euler, simple, CFG 1, the settings from ComfyUI's own template.
  • VAE Decode - Turns the finished render into a picture.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Image Compare Pixaroma - Your picture and the result, one over the other. Move the mouse across it to slide between them: with the LoRA on, the lines of the painting sit on the lines of the photo.
  • Preview Image Pixaroma - Shows the result and saves it to your output folder as a PNG.

The dark Run Timer above them shows how long the last Run took.

widgets_values:
{"version": 1, "content": "

SETTINGS AND RUN TIME

 What this workflow makes

Your picture in a new style, drawn on its own frame: here, the terrace turned into a watercolor painting with every window, the door and the chair where they were, so it lines up with the photo in the Compare.

Every number below was measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow and its own settings, each run on a fresh seed with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the cost goes up with the pixels.

 What the LoRA changes

Ask plain Qwen Image 2.1 for a new style and the result often comes back a little bigger, taller or nudged sideways, different on every seed, so it no longer lines up with your picture. The Consistency LoRA makes the edit on your picture's own frame.

Measured on this workflow's demo, the same 8 seeds with the LoRA row on and off, lining each painting up with the photo and checking how far its corners moved: without the LoRA the median was 21 px and the worst 72 px, with one painting drawn 7.7% bigger than the photo. With it the median was 2 px and the worst 14 px.

Its maker tested it at about 1 megapixel. Here it also held at the bigger sizes: at 1536 and 2048 the paintings stayed within 5 px of the photo.

To see it yourself, switch the LoRA row off, Run the same seed, and slide the Compare.

LoRA model card 

 How long a Run takes

Output SizeResultNew picture or promptNew seed only
1024 - about 1 MP1024 x 10248 s6 s
1536 - about 2.4 MP1536 x 153621 s18 s
2048 - native 2K2048 x 204848 s40 s

The result sizes are for a square picture like the demo one. Change the picture or the prompt and the model reads the picture again, which is the first time column. Change only the seed and it reuses what it read, which is the second.

The Output Size is what costs you: 2048 took about six times as long as 1024. Try your prompt at 1024 and go up once you like the result.

 Why the picture is trimmed a little

The model works in steps of 32 pixels, and most pictures do not divide evenly. Qwen's text encoder on its own stretches the picture to the nearest size that does, by up to about 2 percent (0.9 percent on a 4:3 photo), and the result then comes out slightly wider or narrower than your picture. Here the helpers crop instead of stretching: a thin strip, usually a few pixels, comes off two opposite edges, and the result keeps the exact proportions and lines up in the Compare.

 Kitchen attention

The teal Model Attention Backend node is set to comfy kitchen attention, a faster way to do the attention maths. On the same seed at Output Size 2048, it took 40 s, against 1 min 04 s with the normal pytorch attention, and the two pictures came out practically the same. To compare it yourself, switch the node to pytorch attention.

It needs an Nvidia or AMD graphics card. On anything else ComfyUI falls back to normal attention by itself, so the workflow still runs.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI has to load 6.8 GB of image model and 8.7 GB of text encoder. Measured on a 1024 edit: 12 s with the models unloaded first, 7 s once they were loaded.

That was with the model files still in this machine's file cache. The very first load after switching the computer on reads them off the disk for real and will be slower; that case was not measured, so no number is given for it.

 What it takes off the card

The graphics card peaked at about 22 GB during these runs, at Output Size 2048. ComfyUI keeps the models loaded while it has room, so that number says a 24 GB card copes, not how little the model can get by with.

 The memory node (Qwen Image 2.1 Cache)

While it renders, the model keeps what it has worked out about your picture and the prompt in a cache, so it does not redo that on every step. The teal node says where that cache lives. Leave it on auto / default: auto keeps the cache in spare graphics memory and moves it to system RAM when that runs out.

On a smaller card, if an edit is slow, try dtype int8. It halves the cache, and the node's own description says that can speed an edit up when memory is short. On this 24 GB card it made no difference (41 s against 40 s at 2048). Setting device to cpu, which keeps the cache in system RAM all the time, also cost nothing here (39 s).

 Writing the prompt

  • Name the style plainly: Turn this photo into a watercolor painting. An oil painting, a pencil sketch or a comic book style work the same way.
  • The LoRA keeps the picture in place; it does not make a weak edit stronger. If plain Qwen will not do an edit, this will not either.
  • It was trained on English instructions.
  • For a small change to one area, like a new colour on one object, the Sketch and Inpaint workflows in this folder target it directly.

Tested on 8 seeds: every one came out as a watercolor of the terrace, with the door, the window, the chair and the plant where they are in the photo.
